cacophony

/kuh-KAH-fuh-nee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Cacophony means a harsh, jarring mixture of loud, discordant sounds.

When the parrots, the barking puppies, and the squeaky exercise wheels all started up at once, the pet store filled with a cacophony that sent customers hurrying back out the door.

Example

Five minutes before rehearsal, the middle school band room erupted: trumpets blatted scales, drummers pounded on rims, and a clarinet shrieked its highest note, a cacophony that made the director cover her ears.

Every instrument is producing its own loud sound at the same time, with nothing blending or harmonizing. That jumbled, grating wall of clashing noise is exactly what cacophony names.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

din: A din is a loud, unpleasant noise that goes on and on, like the din of highway traffic. Its defining feature is sheer relentless volume. A cacophony is defined instead by clash: many sounds fighting one another, harsh and discordant even when none of them is very loud.

clamor: Clamor is the loud outcry of many people, a crowd of voices shouting at once, often demanding something. A cacophony need not involve voices or demands at all: it is any harsh, grating mix of clashing, discordant sounds, human or not.

racket: A racket is a loud, disturbing noise, like the neighbors' racket at midnight. Like a din, a racket is measured in volume and annoyance. A cacophony is measured in discord, in how badly the sounds clash, which is why even a quiet cacophony grates on the ear.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

harmony: a pleasing, orderly combination of sounds

hush: a silence or stillness

Where it sits · how loud and disorderly the sound gets

noise → cacophony → pandemonium

noise vs. cacophony: Noise is any unwanted sound, even a single humming fan; a cacophony is a whole tangle of loud, clashing sounds hitting the ear at once.

pandemonium vs. cacophony: Pandemonium goes beyond cacophony, adding wild, uncontrolled chaos and confusion on top of the deafening sound.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — caco-: bad, harsh (Greek kakos)

Root — phon: sound, voice (Greek phone)

Suffix — -y: forms a noun naming a state or quality

Put it together: Caco- (bad) plus phon (sound) literally builds 'bad sound.' Add the noun ending -y and you get cacophony, the name for a harsh, ugly mix of sounds.

Use the root in a new word: symphony: The orchestra's new symphony filled the hall for nearly an hour, and the audience sat spellbound to the final note.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / descriptive

Cacophony most often appears in the pattern 'a cacophony of' followed by the sound sources, as in 'a cacophony of horns' or 'a cacophony of voices.' Do not confuse it with symphony, which shares the 'sound' root but names organized, harmonious sound; a cacophony is the opposite, sound with no order or blend at all.
